topic: Shell exit from Phase 2 and YPF/Eni/XRG consolidation of Phase 3
wiki_text: In December 2025 Shell withdrew from the YPF-led phase of Argentina LNG it had joined only in December 2024, citing a 'significant change in the project scope' after that phase was downsized from a 12 mtpa target to about 6 mtpa. Shell had participated only through the pre-FEED stage and opted not to advance to the next phase; YPF said it would seek a new partner for the scaled-down phase. In parallel, the separate Eni-led phase was elevated as the priority development track: on 12 February 2026 YPF, Eni and XRG (the international energy investment company of Abu Dhabi's ADNOC) signed a binding Joint Development Agreement to advance that phase — 12 mtpa via two floating LNG units of 6 mtpa each — moving into FEED with a final investment decision targeted for the second half of 2026 and first exports expected in 2030-2031. YPF's CEO indicated the three partners would hold roughly a third each, though final equity stakes were not formalized.

topic: Phase 1 (Southern Energy) progress and SEFE offtake — first long-term LNG export contract
wiki_text: Southern Energy SA (SESA) — owned by Pan American Energy (30%), YPF (25%), Pampa Energia (20%), Harbour Energy (15%) and Golar LNG (10%) — reached FID on Phase 1 in 2025, comprising two chartered Golar FLNG units: the Hilli Episeyo (2.45 mtpa, restart expected 2027) and the MKII conversion (3.5 mtpa, deployment expected 2028), for a combined ~5.95 mtpa. The Hilli Episeyo is due to enter Seatrium's Singapore yard in Q3 2026 for life-extension, winterization and a new soft-yoke mooring before deployment to the Gulf of San Matias, Rio Negro. In March 2026 Germany's SEFE (Securing Energy for Europe) finalized an 8-year sales-and-purchase agreement to buy 2 mtpa FOB from SESA starting late 2027 — about one third of Phase 1's output and described as Argentina's first long-term LNG export contract. Golar has signalled it aims to order a 4th FLNG within 2026 as the commercial pipeline expands.

YPF has engaged JP Morgan to raise up to US$16 billion in project financing for the roughly US$20 billion Eni-led Phase 3 of Argentina LNG (YPF/Eni/XRG, 12 mtpa via two 6-mtpa FLNG units), targeting a final investment decision in the second half of 2026 and first exports around 2030-2031. The phase advanced through a binding Joint Development Agreement signed 12 February 2026, following Eni's signature of the technical framework in October 2025.
